newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to load more wheat for Iraq this week.
newsitem.headline: France to load more wheat for Iraq this week.

text.p: The northern French port of Rouen is expected to load its first cargo of wheat for Iraq under a United Nations oil-for-food scheme at the end of this week, freight sources said.
Grain freighter Freedom K is anchored outside the port and plans to berth by the end of the week to load 23,350 tonnes of wheat for distribution in Iraq, they said.
France has sold 600,000 tonnes of wheat to Iraq under the U.N. plan to ease Gulf War sanctions by raising money for humanitarian supplies of food and medicine through oil sales.
Of this total, France has so far sought U.N. approval for 300,000 tonnes and has received the go-ahead for two contracts covering 200,000 tonnes, a budget ministry official said.
On Monday, the western French port of Nantes began loading 25,000 tonnes for Iraq under the same U.N. scheme, freight officials there said.
Unconfirmed market reports said the same port had also loaded 35,000 tonnes for Iraq in mid-February.
On February 19, the United Nations said it had given the necessary approval for eight international contracts to supply food to Iraq, including French wheat worth $21 million.
